name: MS-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a 14-point Republican partisan lean
Incumbent Michael Guest running with a large financial advantage ($962K on hand vs $23K)
No public polling and no expert ratings, leaving fundamentals as the main guide
Prediction markets price Guest at roughly 98% to win
model.rationale: Guest holds a seat with a 14-point Republican lean, faces a minimally funded challenger, and markets price his reelection near 98 percent. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, this stays safely Republican.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the challenger within single digits, or significant outside spending against Guest, would be the first sign this is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mississippi's 3rd District is a solidly Republican seat, and incumbent Michael Guest is seeking another term after easily securing his party's nomination. His Democratic challenger, Michael Chiaradio, has raised about $155,000 and had roughly $23,000 on hand, while Guest has raised over $820,000 and holds nearly $1 million in cash. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's 14-point Republican lean, Guest's incumbency and financial edge, and prediction markets that price his chances near 98 percent. The race is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling rather than any evidence of competition.
